correctness.rationale: Under fixed known 0<f<p<1, derive no-positive probability u_t=ψ(1−p)^t+(1−ψ)(1−f)^t, OR information Δ_t²/[u_t(1−u_t)] and exact cost H_t. At fixed ε>0 information per visit tends to zero; at ψ→1, boundary score grows as (b²/a)^t/t. When a≥b² a uniform 1/t envelope keeps maximizers bounded, including equality; when a<b² boundary score rules out bounded maximizers. Exact two-exponential expression for H_t, coercivity outside t=L/log(b/a)+O(1), and uniform asymptotic inside give the lattice periodic Φ. Full histories at ψ=1 give chi-square K^t−1 with K=f²/p+b²/a>1; complete-data information bounds every interior score, proving finite maximizers and their divergence near ψ=1. Recomputed exact rational full-vs-OR Fisher information and boundary chi-square in 21 tests. Infinite claims follow from these inequalities, not finite sampling.
residual_risks: Finite rational checks cannot prove asymptotic minimizer localization.
Fixed-budget interpretation and one-sided prevalence limit must be kept distinct.

value.rationale: Near-ubiquity design is a natural limiting stress case for replicated ecological detection; coarsening full visits to one OR bit is a practical, mathematically motivated information loss. The dichotomy p≤2f−f² versus p>2f−f², divergent full-history optimal replication, and integer-phase exact variance are sharp actionable structural features not mere numerical maximizer examples. Model scope fixed rates is clearly stated.
residual_risks: Survey overhead/travel and estimated p,f may change applied optimum; value is mathematical local benchmark.

limitations: Known calibrated p,f and conditional independent visits/site occupancy; asymptotic ψ↑1, exact untruncated variance and infinite-budget local information criterion. McClish–Quade 1985 full text inaccessible after VPN disconnect; uncertain older priority.
